title: Here, bhikkhus, knowing a person's mind as defiled with my own mind, I understand: 'If this person were to die at this time, he would…
content: Here, bhikkhus, knowing a person's mind as defiled with my own mind, I understand: 'If this person were to die at this time, he would be reborn in hell accordingly.' Why is that? Because his mind is defiled. It is because of a defiled mind, bhikkhus, that some beings here, after death, with the breakup of the body, are reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell.

title: Bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu practice the things proper to a samaṇa? He abides pervading one direction with a mind imbued with loving-kindness... compassion... altruistic…
content: Bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu practice the things proper to a samaṇa? He abides pervading one direction with a mind imbued with loving-kindness... compassion... altruistic joy... equanimity, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, across, everywhere, in all respects, he abides pervading the entire world with a mind imbued with equanimity, vast, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill-will. Bhikkhus, just as a lotus pond with clear, sweet, cool, limpid water, with beautifully arranged banks, is delightful — if a person comes from the east, overcome and afflicted by heat, exhausted, parched, and thirsty, and goes to that pond, he would quench his thirst and cool his heat... if a person comes from the west... from the north... from the south... from anywhere, overcome by heat, afflicted, exhausted, parched, and thirsty, and goes to that pond, he would quench his thirst and cool his heat. So too, bhikkhus, if a person from the noble warrior caste goes forth from home to homelessness and comes to the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata, and having developed loving-kindness, compassion, altruistic joy, and equanimity, attains inner concentration — I say that through this inner concentration he practices the things proper to a samaṇa.

title: Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu reviles, criticizes, or reproaches the noble ones who are his fellow celibates, it is impossible, there is no chance that he…
content: Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu reviles, criticizes, or reproaches the noble ones who are his fellow celibates, it is impossible, there is no chance that he will not encounter one of eleven misfortunes. What eleven? He does not attain what has not been attained; what has been attained he loses; the true Dhamma is not made clear to him; or he becomes puffed up in the true Dhamma; or he does not delight in living the holy life; or he commits a defiled offense; or he gives up the holy life and returns to the lower life; or he contracts a severe illness; or he becomes mad or mentally deranged; or he dies confused; or after death, with the breakup of the body, he falls into a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu reviles, criticizes, or reproaches the noble ones who are his fellow celibates, it is impossible, there is no chance that he will not encounter one of these eleven misfortunes.

title: There are these five dangers, bhikkhus, for a person without serene confidence. What five? Those without faith are not inspired; some who have faith may…
content: There are these five dangers, bhikkhus, for a person without serene confidence. What five? Those without faith are not inspired; some who have faith may change; he does not follow the Teacher's instruction; later generations follow wrong view; his mind is not serene. Bhikkhus, these are the five dangers for a person without serene confidence.

title: Great King, just as a man with a multi-storied mansion with an upper terrace at a crossroads, standing there, would see people entering houses, leaving…
content: Great King, just as a man with a multi-storied mansion with an upper terrace at a crossroads, standing there, would see people entering houses, leaving houses, walking back and forth on the road, sitting at the crossroads or on the upper terrace. He would think: 'These people are entering houses, these are leaving houses, these are walking back and forth on the road, these are sitting at the crossroads, on the upper terrace.' So too, Great King, with his mind thus concentrated, purified, bright, unblemished, free from defilements, pliant, workable, steady, and imperturbable, the bhikkhu directs his mind to the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings. With the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees beings passing away and being reborn.

title: Here, friends, greed is an unwholesome state, and hatred is also an unwholesome state. There is a Middle Way that abandons greed and abandons hatred,…
content: Here, friends, greed is an unwholesome state, and hatred is also an unwholesome state. There is a Middle Way that abandons greed and abandons hatred, giving rise to (pure) vision, giving rise to (true) knowledge, leading to peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, Nibbāna. And what, friends, is that Middle Way — (the way) that gives rise to (pure) vision, gives rise to (true) knowledge, leading to peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, Nibbāna? It is the Noble Eightfold Path, namely: Right View, Right Intention, Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, Right Concentration. Friends, this is that Middle Way, giving rise to (pure) vision, giving rise to (true) knowledge, leading to peace, direct knowledge, enlightenment, Nibbāna.

title: Thus Samaṇa Gotama unites those who are divided, encourages those who are united, delights in harmony, rejoices in harmony, speaks words that lead to harmony.…
content: Thus Samaṇa Gotama unites those who are divided, encourages those who are united, delights in harmony, rejoices in harmony, speaks words that lead to harmony. Bhikkhus, Samaṇa Gotama abstains from harsh speech, avoids harsh speech; he speaks words that are blameless, pleasing to the ear, affectionate, touching the heart, courteous, delightful to many, agreeable to many. Samaṇa Gotama speaks such words.

title: So too, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, in accordance with Dhamma, the Dhamma-King, relying on Dhamma, honoring Dhamma, respecting Dhamma, venerating…
content: So too, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, in accordance with Dhamma, the Dhamma-King, relying on Dhamma, honoring Dhamma, respecting Dhamma, venerating Dhamma, having Dhamma as his banner, having Dhamma as his flag, having Dhamma as his supremacy, gives protection, shelter, and support in accordance with Dhamma regarding bodily action, thinking: 'Such bodily action should be practiced, such bodily action should not be practiced.' Furthermore, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata... gives protection, shelter, and support in accordance with Dhamma regarding verbal action, thinking: 'Such verbal action should be practiced, such verbal action should not be practiced'; regarding mental action, thinking: 'Such mental action should be practiced, such mental action should not be practiced.' That Tathāgata... having given protection, shelter, and support... regarding bodily action, verbal action, mental action, sets in motion the wheel of Dhamma. That wheel is not to be turned back by any ascetic, brahmin, deva, Māra, Brahmā, or anyone in the world.

title: 'The world, the world,' Venerable Sir, is said. To what extent, Venerable Sir, is there the world or the concept of the world?" - "Where,…
content: 'The world, the world,' Venerable Sir, is said. To what extent, Venerable Sir, is there the world or the concept of the world?" - "Where, Samiddhi, there is the eye, there are forms, there is eye-consciousness, there are things cognizable by the eye — there the world or the concept of the world exists. ... Where there is the mind, there are mind-objects, there is mind-consciousness, there are things cognizable by the mind — there the world or the concept of the world exists. And where, Samiddhi, there is no eye, no forms, no eye-consciousness, no things cognizable by the eye — there the world or the concept of the world does not exist. ... Where there is no mind, no mind-objects, no mind-consciousness, no things cognizable by the mind — there the world or the concept of the world does not exist.

title: Furthermore, wanderers, the brahmin says thus: 'I am not anyone's, not anything's anywhere, nor am I anything anywhere. There is nothing belonging to me anywhere,…
content: Furthermore, wanderers, the brahmin says thus: 'I am not anyone's, not anything's anywhere, nor am I anything anywhere. There is nothing belonging to me anywhere, in any way.' The brahmin who says this speaks the truth, not falsehood. Therefore, he does not think of 'ascetic,' does not think of 'brahmin,' does not think 'I am superior,' does not think 'I am equal,' does not think 'I am inferior.' Furthermore, by directly knowing the truth contained therein, he practices the path of nothingness.
